title: Knicks’ announcement means bad news for everybody, including New York
author: Kento Kato
text:
Not the news Knicks fans wanted to hear.

While the Knicks and their fans have spent much of the summer celebrating their first championship in 53 years, the upcoming contract situations of a few players have loomed over their heads. And if said players wanted to secure their futures before the start of the season, they were in for a good dose of bad news on Friday.

Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart, Miles McBride, and Tyler Kolek all are extension eligible. Hart was asked about his future at the start of training camp and left the door open to anything. Towns and his on going negotiation’s progress, or lack there of, have taken over the news lately. And for good reason.

Many still believe that the two sides will eventually come together for a deal. But the fact that they are reportedly not even close is a bit concerning. Towns, as was on full display during the team’s championship run, is an incredibly pivotal part of the Knicks’ success. Losing him would be devastating as his shooting gravity and playmaking would be extremely difficult to replace. As if not being able to extend Town wasn’t bad enough though, the Knicks don’t seem close at all to really extending any of the other players as well either. And according to the Knicks themselves, it will remain that way for the foreseeable future.

We’ve all seen players make statements about how they want to hold off contract talks when the season begins because they want to focus solely on the upcoming season. But in a rare move, the Knicks were the ones to get ahead of the news and release an official statement .

“As an organization, our entire focus is on preparing for the upcoming season and delivering another year for our fans to be proud of,” a spokesperson from the Knicks said. “As a result, we will not be negotiating contract extensions until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season.”

Again, it’s rare for a team to be the one to make this statement. And it’s a bit frightening for fans knowing that such important pieces of the core’s future remains largely unknown. One would like to believe that between Towns’, Hart’s, and McBride’s significance to the club and their desire to stay a Knick we’d have some clearer answers by now.

The second apron continues to loom large so it’s understandable, realistic, and arguably smarter to not extend all three. McBride, unfortunately, was likely playing his last season here regardless of how these extensions went. But to potentially have a future where all, or at least more than one of them, aren’t Knicks would quickly lower the ceiling of this team. The Knicks still would have a core of Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, and OG Anunoby, along with Jose Alvarado, Landry Shamet, and Mohamed Diawara. But the Knicks are a significantly worse team without Towns and to a lesser degree, without Hart and McBride.

It’s not time for full on panic. Things like this have happened in the past with other negotiations, with everything eventually working out. It could also just be a leverage move. And the most important part is, all parties involved want to extend the marriage.

All that being said, it is hard to deny just how ominous of a start this is for a franchise coming off it’s highest of highs and looking to become the first team to win back-to-back championships for the first time in 53 years.

title: Trump Warns Norway He Won’t Forget Nobel Peace Prize Snub
author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Catherine Lucey
text: President Donald Trump fumed at the Norwegian committee that awards the Nobel Peace Prize, saying that the fact it didn’t go to him “is just another sign of how Norway and all these others are ripping off our country.”

title: Trump fumes over Nobel peace prize snub and criticizes Norway
author: Robert Mackey
text:
President complains about not winning prize in year he started war with Iran and says: ‘We will not forget, Norway’

Donald Trump complained Friday about not winning the Nobel peace prize for 2026, a year in which he started a war with Iran.

At what was supposed to be a rally for other Republican candidates in Syracuse, New York, the US president devoted a long portion of his speech airing his grievances with the Nobel committee.

“The United States of America, represented by me as your president, should have received the Nobel peace prize, but didn’t. And this is an indelible stain on the country of Norway , and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision,” Trump said.

“The Nobel peace prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilization,” Trump went on. “We will not forget, Norway, that you didn’t give this prize.”

Trump also recited a list of wars he claims to have settled, some of which were not wars and some that are still not settled, before adding: “I’m about to settle or win two more: Iran and Russia-Ukraine.”

Trump said he would be ending both wars “quickly”.

“I will tell you what,” he added, darkly. “Iran will be very quick one way or the other: that they give us everything or they don’t exist any longer.”

“Additionally, I stopped Iran from having a nuclear weapon and blowing up the entire Middle East and ultimately far beyond the Middle East, including Europe, perhaps the US and I saved more lives than anyone in history,” Trump claimed, despite the fact that US intelligence agencies reported to Congress in 2025 that Iran had actually suspended its pursuit of nuclear weapons in 2003.

“Despite all of this and all of these unbelievable accomplishments, the Nobel prize was given out today to a liberal person who works at the United Nations, who nobody has ever heard of,” Trump said of Navi Pillay , the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza.

title: As it happened: Late crash sees Dutch dominance continue in women's UCI Gravel World Championships on muddy course
author: Tim Bonville-Ginn
text:
Marianne Vos went solo over the top of the final climb with Rosa Klöser crashing as she tried to follow. Larissa Hartop outsprinted Nele Laing to take bronze.

1. Marianne Vos (NED) 4:30'04"2. Rosa Klöser (GER) +27" 3. Larissa Hartog (NED) +2'15"

4. Nele Laing (GER) S.T. 5. Erica Magnaldi (ITA) +4'17"

6. Sofía Gómez Villafañe (ARG) +5'15" 7. Irina Lützelschwab (SWI) +5'28"

8. Tiffany Cromwell (AUS) +7'15" 9. Elisa Serné (NED) S.T.

10. Haley Smith (CAN) +8'55"

The temperatures have been high for much of the week but it is a cool and fresh 16°C, unusually low for spring time in the area.

October 9, 2026 – 9:24 PM Hello and welcome to ' live updates of the women's UCI World Gravel Championships 2026 from Nannup, Western Australia.

October 9, 2026 – 9:28 PM Info from our Australia Editor Simone Giuliani on the ground is that the course has had some overnight rain, compacting the pea gravel making the route less slippery.

However, the riders will have to contend with puddles, likely not to the same extent seen at Unbound this year, but still an extra challenge for the riders.

October 9, 2026 – 9:35 PM The women face a challenging but rather short 125.6km of racing on the gravel of Western Australia, what should they be looking out for? Well, we've put together what we think will be the three things that could shape the racing...

October 9, 2026 – 9:39 PM Racing is due to begin at 10:10 local time in Nannup. Roughly 30 minutes from now.

October 9, 2026 – 9:48 PM For those who may not be familiar with the gravel scene but knows road will have one name screaming out at them, that being former world gravel champion Marianne Vos. However, there are some star specialists are here with Argentina's Sofia Gomez Villafañe, home rider Nicole Frain and many more all lining up to challenge.

October 9, 2026 – 9:53 PM The course itself is extremely challenging. While it is rather short, in the 125.6km of racing there are 3180 metres of elevation gain with the climbs not allow immediate rest after the summits are they tend to plateau for a while afterwards.

October 9, 2026 – 9:55 PM The gravel is like nothing seen in European gravel racing and is unique to the area in Australia. Pea gravel is what it says on the tin, gravel that is shaped like peas. It can been incredibly slippery when dry but when wet it can be compacted down and become less notable with tyre choice being crucial.

October 9, 2026 – 9:58 PM The riders are beginning to line up on the start line in Nannup with Wendy Oosterwoud of the Netherlands wearing number one.

October 9, 2026 – 10:04 PM It is being said that this is a 'true' gravel course with 85% of the course on gravel with intense gradients and a huge amount of climbing. The chance for the specialists to finally have a pure gravel rider in the rainbow bands after road stars have dominated the first four editions.

October 9, 2026 – 10:06 PM This will be the final race in the career of South African WorldTour rider Ashleigh Moolman-Pasio despite having a cold.

October 9, 2026 – 10:08 PM Australian gravel champion and winner here for the SEVEN Gravel race in Nannup earlier in the year, Tiffany Cromwell, is another rider who will be hanging up the wheels after this race.

October 9, 2026 – 10:10 PM Racing begins for the 2026 Gravel World Championships in Nannup with the Dutch team immediately up to the front.

October 9, 2026 – 10:13 PM It is a fast start on the asphalt to begin with the tiny peloton bunched together for the moment but when they hit the gravel it'll likely immediately split up.

October 9, 2026 – 10:18 PM The home nation gets the ball rolling with the first attack of the day. No-one keen on following for the time being as we are still on the asphalt with 10km until the gravel begins.

October 9, 2026 – 10:19 PM 12 riders down as DNFs including Germany's Romy Kaspar and the Netherlands' Riejanne Markus.

October 9, 2026 – 10:23 PM Bloor has a gap of just 12" on the peloton as the gravel edges closer and closer.

October 9, 2026 – 10:27 PM Bloor leads onto the gravel with a very wet surface and a few puddles. A couple of early twitches from the back wheel for the Australian rider. She now has 34" on the peloton.

October 9, 2026 – 10:28 PM The peloton hit the gravel and immediately things change as the pace shoots up with the Dutch crowding the front still. 5km to the first climb of the day.

October 9, 2026 – 10:30 PM Bloor's wheel skipping and skidding all over the place forcing her to freewheel. All the riders have only been able to recon some of the route due to some of the sections being on private property including the first climb of the day.

October 9, 2026 – 10:32 PM Mud is already caking the backs of the riders as the riders are on the first climb of the day now.

October 9, 2026 – 10:34 PM Mutsumi Hara (Japan) and Elizabeth Hermolle (Great Britain) early off the back but it is a tough start and there's a long way to go as the rain begins to fall again.

October 9, 2026 – 10:40 PM The gap goes out to a minute for Bloor who will be very happy for the moment but I imagine she would like to have some company. She rides solo for the time being.

October 9, 2026 – 10:40 PM The climb Killarney which is 5.4km of very undulating riding and an average of 3.4% but with some nasty kickers.

October 9, 2026 – 10:43 PM Multiple riders now struggling to hold onto the peloton as Bloor has 1'02" on the pack.

October 9, 2026 – 10:46 PM One unexpected rider on the startlist for the elite women was Peta Mullens (Australia) who was expecting to ride the age group of 35-39 but received an email a few days ago saying she will have to race the elite due to rule changes coming into force...

October 9, 2026 – 10:46 PM Bloor's gap has now reduced significantly as she continues to tap out a rhythm that suits her but she now just has 30" on the chasers.

October 9, 2026 – 10:47 PM The peloton has shrunk quite a lot on this first climb with Bloor being reeled back in very soon.

October 9, 2026 – 10:50 PM Former Australian national road champion Nicole Frain is keen to see a gravel specialist take the title today...

October 9, 2026 – 10:52 PM Not ideal for the Irish rider who clipped a wheel and came down. She is back riding but is now out of the back.

October 9, 2026 – 10:53 PM Inside 1km from the top of the Killarney climb as Bloor holds a very slender lead.

October 9, 2026 – 10:55 PM Bloor is caught by the Dutch led peloton that has been whittled right down on the first climb.

October 9, 2026 – 10:56 PM Onto the first descent of the day now and the pace shot up to make sure they were in a good position with Vos, Sophie Wright (Great Britain) and Larissa Hartog (Netherlands) leading the way.

October 9, 2026 – 10:57 PM The sun is back out now but the gravel is very wet and slippy.

October 9, 2026 – 10:59 PM One of the big favourites for the race is trying to fix this quickly with her plugs but the sealant taking a while. She is now back riding but a long way out the back now. Similar happened in Unbound earlier this year.

October 9, 2026 – 11:00 PM Some info coming from the start... The age groupers are heading out in waves now. Some were so keen to ensure a good spot in the start line that they were sitting in the ground with their bikes in their start box well over an hour before their start time.

October 9, 2026 – 11:03 PM Maddy Nutt (Great Britain) was just off the back after that descent but has made it back in now. She will be relying on her huge engine and stamina to be involved in the final...

October 9, 2026 – 11:05 PM The peloton now bunches up after that descent as they build towards the first majorly hard climb of Brockwell.

October 9, 2026 – 11:05 PM Wright, Hartog, Cromwell and Erica Magnaldi (Italy) lead the peloton on this rolling terrain.

October 9, 2026 – 11:09 PM Onto the Brockman climb with Wright and Magnaldi upping the tempo with the rain starting yet again. You won't win the race here but you can certainly lose it.

October 9, 2026 – 11:10 PM The climb is 2.5km at 8% with kicks well over 15%.

October 9, 2026 – 11:11 PM Klöser has fought very well and is about 10" off the back of the lead group and is picking up riders who are losing touch.

October 9, 2026 – 11:13 PM Wright is ripping this peloton to bits on this climb but Klöser is about to make it back on.

October 9, 2026 – 11:14 PM Klöser flies pass British duo of Nutt and Hermolle as they have to negotiate their way around one of the camera bikes that has got stuck in the mud on the gradients of Brockman.

October 9, 2026 – 11:15 PM Wendy Oosterwoud (Netherlands), Gravel World Series leader, has been gapped just before the hardest section. That is a big surprise.

October 9, 2026 – 11:16 PM Cromwell also out of the back with Denmark's Janni Spangsberg Schori losing tough as well.

October 9, 2026 – 11:17 PM The Dutch still just about have four riders in this select group with Hartog and Geerike Schreurs just holding on.

October 9, 2026 – 11:21 PM Sofía Gómez Villafañe (Argentina)Nicole Frain (Australia) Marianne Vos (Netherlands)

Ashleigh Moolman-Pasio (South Africa) Erica Magnaldi (Italy) Elisa Serné (Netherlands)

Rosa Klöser (Germany) Geerike Schreurs (Netherlands)

Larissa Hartog (Netherlanda) Irina Lützelschwab (Switzerland)

Haley Smith (Canada)

And a few others now lead.

October 9, 2026 – 11:21 PM Wright did all that work on the toughest gradients but has not made the group.

October 9, 2026 – 11:22 PM Cromwell, Wright, Oosterwoud are now around 45" down on the leaders.

October 9, 2026 – 11:23 PM Through the feed zone now as multiple riders take on fresh bottles, bars and gels.

October 9, 2026 – 11:24 PM Great crowds around the feed area after a period on private land.

October 9, 2026 – 11:24 PM On the Adina climb now, 1.1km long at 4% average.

October 9, 2026 – 11:27 PM Bit of grass racing turns into mud and then some more traditional looking gravel for a very short period before returning back to the pea gravel very soon.

October 9, 2026 – 11:30 PM She has a front flat but she seems to have got it fixed pretty fast.

October 9, 2026 – 11:35 PM The gap between the lead group including Vos, Villafañe, Klöser, Moolman-Pasio and the rest have a minute on the group including Cromwell, Wright and Oosterwoud.

October 9, 2026 – 11:37 PM Onto Shale climb of 800m at 6.8% which is being done very swiftly as Villafañe and Magnaldi lead the way for now.

October 9, 2026 – 11:42 PM The Shale climb appears to have favoured the chase group as the gap drops to 22", but this will be based on the motorbikes so we take that gap with a pinch of salt.

October 9, 2026 – 11:43 PM And the gap is closing. 15" between the leaders and chasers as riders like Cromwell, Oosterwoud and Flora Johnson (Great Britain) may get back in.

October 9, 2026 – 11:45 PM Cromwell is leading the chasing group back to the front group as the leader's pace lulls. That was a big effort from the chasers with Oosterwoud still struggling to hold the wheel but we now have a lead group of around 16 riders.

October 9, 2026 – 11:47 PM Tiffany Cromwell (Australia)

The Australian champion launches as soon as she re-joined the leaders to try and get clear but she is solo and the chase is on.

October 9, 2026 – 11:50 PM Vos tried a move but she was heavily marked. Cromwell continues to press on as the chase group starts to sit up a bit more.

October 9, 2026 – 11:52 PM Magnaldi is investing a lot of energy on the front of the favourites group without dropping anyone but they stall again and allow Cromwell a bit more gap.

October 9, 2026 – 11:53 PM Cromwell expands her lead to 10" as the chase stalls.

October 9, 2026 – 11:54 PM Marianne Vos (Netherlands)

The former world champion launches for a second time to try and close Cromwell down. She is marked but it has got the rest of the group interested in chasing again.…

title: Three men found guilty of murders of Australian surfer brothers and US friend in Mexico
author: Graham Readfearn and Agence France-Press
text:
Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, 30 and 33, and friend Carter Rhoad, 30, were killed on a surfing trip in 2024

Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast

The parents of Australian surfing brothers murdered in Mexico have said “no outcome can ever undo this tragedy” after three men were convicted of the 2024 killings.

Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33 respectively, and their friend Carter Rhoad, 30, were on a surfing trip to Mexico’s Pacific coast when they were shot dead in Baja California state in a suspected robbery.

The deaths of the trio sparked an outpouring of grief and condemnation in Australia and the United States.

Jesus Gerardo – known as “El Kekas” – was accused of leading the attack. His surname has not been disclosed for legal reasons. He and two other defendants, Irineo Francisco and Angel Jesus, were found guilty on Friday local time.

The judge ruled the three Mexican defendants acted with premeditation.

Martin and Debra Robinson, the brothers’ parents, travelled from Australia to the port city of Ensenada for the trial, which began on 7 September.

“They took our sons from our lives forever,” said Debra Robinson, who testified on the final day of the trial. “What hurts us most is that, in their final hours, they were treated with such cruelty.”

She burst into tears when the guilty verdict was pronounced.

Speaking outside the court after the verdict, Martin Robinson thanked family and friends for their support, and also thanked the judge, court staff, the Australian embassy in Mexico and the Australian federal police.

He said: “No outcome can ever undo this tragedy, but we hope today marks an important step towards justice and allows us to continue honouring their lives and the extraordinary young men they were. They will never be forgotten.”

Debra Robinson said: “I don’t feel any different today as I did yesterday or I will tomorrow, because … Callum and Jake are not here. A verdict is a good thing, but it doesn’t bring them back.”

She said she had no feelings towards the three guilty men. “I have tried to hold on to the memory of my children, my sons, and I try really not to think about them. And I don’t actually want them to have any notoriety. We don’t actually really speak their names. They’re not part of our grief really.”

Martin Robinson said a foundation in their sons’ names would carry on their legacy.

The Callum and Jake Robinson Foundation aims to “help people live bigger, shine brighter and love harder in their honour”.

Rhoad’s mother, Page, and his fiance, Natalie Weirtz, also participated in the hearing in a video call from the United States.

“The accused are guilty and must be punished so that no other family suffers the same pain,” Weirtz said. “Since Carter’s death, I feel paranoid and isolated.”

The prosecution requested 210 years’ imprisonment for each of the accused, though the maximum sentence in Baja California is 60 years.

The surfers were camping in a remote beachside area when they were attacked in April 2024. Their bodies were found in a clifftop shaft, with gunshot wounds to their heads.

In November 2025, Ary Gisell Silva , the then-girlfriend of the main defendant, was sentenced to two decades in prison after admitting that she instigated the robbery.

Baja California is one of Mexico’s most violent states, plagued by organised crime and drug trafficking, although cartel activity does not usually affect tourists. Other foreign visitors have, however, been targeted in criminal attacks on Mexico’s Pacific coast.

Two Australian surfers, Dean Lucas and Adam Coleman , were killed in 2015 while travelling through the north-western state of Sinaloa. Their bodies were later burned.

title: Powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama and triggers panic in capital
author: Guardian staff and agencies
text:
Hazardous waves are possible as far south as Ecuador and as far north as Mexico, as 13 aftershocks reported

A powerful 7.6 magnitude earthquake has struck Panama and triggered tsunami warnings along the west coast of Central and South America, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS).

The quake hit along the southern coast of the country, the USGS said. It was centered near the southern tip of the Central American country, about 14km (9 miles) south-west of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba, the USGS said.

The Institute of Geosciences of the University of Panama said the quake struck at just before 1pm local time near the southern town of Tonosí. The Panamanian institute said that a second 6.0 magnitude earthquake struck soon after, at 1.22pm.

By 1.3opm there had reportedly been 13 aftershocks.

The president, José Raúl Mulino, said he had asked a key minister to call for calm. “What happened should not be used to generate alarm and disorder,” Mulino wrote on X.

Local newspaper La Prensa said that across the Central American country, buildings, schools and homes were evacuated as a result of the “powerful movement of the earth”.

Footage published by La Prensa showed severe damage to several buildings in the city of Penonomé, including the St John Baptist Cathedral. Other photos showed a highway to the west of the capital that had been completely sheared in half by the earthquake.

Tremors were felt strongly ​in the ⁠capital of ⁠Panama ​City, ‌according ‌to ‌witnesses who spoke to Reuters. The Associated Press reported that buildings shook and visibly shaken residents gathered outside as they waited for news of the quake’s impact.

The USGS said hazardous waves were possible along the coasts of Costa Rica, Ecuador, Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador and Mexico, although the tsunami warning for Chile was cancelled at 4.18pm local time.

title: Anthropic AI Model Went Rogue, Submitted Fake Tip to Police
author: Shirin Ghaffary
text: Anthropic PBC said its Claude AI model carried out additional unintended actions on the digital systems of outside organizations, including submitting a false tip in a police homicide case, prompting a warning from the Trump administration for artificial intelligence companies to secure their systems.
